Impact Statement: Starting at 09:52 UTC on 28 October 2026, a subset of customer using Microsoft Sentinel across multiple regions may experience delays in incident ingestion, processing, and/or incident status updates.

Current Status: We detected this issue through our service monitoring and customer reports. Our investigation found that increased processing demand exceeded the available service resources within a portion of our infrastructure, creating a backlog that caused the delays. Service performance remains improved following our earlier mitigation actions. As processing demand has increased, we have observed a slight rise in backlog and processing latency, and our teams continue to closely monitor service health. To further improve performance, we are progressing two additional mitigation actions focused on increasing processing throughput and reducing the volume of data requiring processing. We expect these measures to help accelerate backlog reduction and further stabilize processing latency. In parallel, we continue to monitor a separate ongoing service issue that may independently contribute to some of the observed latency. We are actively assessing overall service conditions and will continue applying mitigation measures as needed to support recovery.

The next update will be provided within 06 hours, or as events warrant.

properties.description:
What happened?

Between 17:09 UTC and 17:12 UTC on 28 October 2026, a network hardware fault resulted in an impact to a subset of Azure Service in the West Europe region. Impacted customers may have experienced latency, or packet drops when attempting to connect to resources hosted in the West Europe region.


What went wrong, and why?

We determined that, during the brief impact window, a limited number of customers experienced degraded performance due to a transient issue affecting a subset of Azure services in the West Europe region. This transient issue was brought upon by a hardware component, which handles network connections and traffic, stopped working properly. This resulted in a temporary service degradation, manifesting as errors or unsuccessful requests when customers attempted to perform the activities listed above during the time of impact.


How did we respond?

  • 17:09 UTC on 28 October 2026 – Customer impact began.
  • 17:12 UTC on 28 October 2026 – The network protocols automatically routed traffic around the hardware failure. Our team reviewed failure logs and synthetic traffic metrics and determined that no further action is needed, which meant the issue was self-healed. We marked the incident as mitigated and no further impact was identified.


What happens next?

  • This Mitigation Statement is the final communication for this incident. For details about which Azure incidents qualify for which Post Incident Reviews (PIRs), refer to https://aka.ms/AzurePIRs
  • The impact times above represent the full incident duration, so are not specific to any individual customer. Actual impact to service availability may vary between customers and resources – for guidance on implementing monitoring to understand granular impact: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Monitoring
  • To stay informed about future Azure service issues, make sure that you configure and maintain Azure Service Health alerts – these can trigger emails, SMS, push notifications, webhooks, and more: https://aka.ms/ash-alerts
  • For broader guidance on preparing for cloud incidents, refer to https://aka.ms/incidentreadiness
